blocks.text: dockerd runs as root and does whatever its API asks, so anyone who can reach the Docker socket, including every docker group member, effectively has root on the host.

$ docker run --rm -it -v /:/host alpine chroot /host sh   # no sudo needed
# whoami
root
By default, UID 0 in a container is UID 0 on the host kernel. Capabilities, seccomp and AppArmor reduce it, but bind mounts are writable as real root and a kernel escape lands as host root.

rows: Container root → high unprivileged host UID
Daemon itself runs as a normal user
Ports <1024 need sysctl; slower user-space networking; cgroup v2 + systemd delegation for limits

blocks.text: Treat docker group membership like sudo on shared servers and CI runners. Never expose the API on TCP 2375 without TLS: that's unauthenticated remote root.

Q: "Is adding a developer to the docker group safe?" A: "No. The docker group grants socket access, and the socket can start a container that mounts / as root. It's equivalent to passwordless sudo. Use rootless Docker or Podman if that's unacceptable."

items: Socket access = root on the host.
Container root is host UID 0 unless user namespaces remap it.
Always run apps as a non-root USER.
Rootless mode limits blast radius at some networking and feature cost.
